---
title: "Gene Ontology enrichment of isoform-specific AP-MS interactors"
output: html_document
---

## Purpose

Risk- and nonrisk-associated protein isoforms of the 13 CAD sQTL bait pairs were
profiled by affinity-purification mass spectrometry, and every high-confidence
interactor was labelled risk-specific, nonrisk-specific or shared according to
which bait(s) it passed the CompPASS and SAINT thresholds with
(`07_apms_scoring_and_network_annotation.Rmd`). This script asks whether the
isoform-specific interactor sets of each bait pair are enriched for distinct
biological functions, because divergent enrichment between the two isoforms of a
pair is the functional read-out of interactome rewiring. For every bait and each of
the three interactor categories, Gene Ontology Biological Process, Molecular
Function and Cellular Component terms are tested with clusterProfiler (`enrichGO`;
hypergeometric test against the default genome-wide background, Benjamini–Hochberg
correction, *P* < 0.05 and *q* < 0.2; sets with fewer than three mappable genes are
not tested).

Two distinct products are written, because they serve different purposes:

- `pair_by_pair/<BAIT>_pathway_details.csv` holds **all** terms passing the cutoffs
  for every bait × interactor category × ontology. This is the source of
  Supplementary Table 18 and of the per-bait term counts in Fig. 5f.
- `MASTER_pathway_summary.csv` holds the **ten most significant** terms per
  bait × category × ontology. It is used only to select the single GO term that
  labels each bait in the Fig. 5g/h network views, so that labelling follows a
  stated, reproducible rule rather than manual choice.

## Manuscript outputs produced

- Fig. 5f (number of enriched GO terms per bait by interactor category; plotted in
  `10_figure_and_table_generation.Rmd` from the per-bait tables)
- Fig. 5g, 5h (top isoform-specific GO term used to annotate each bait in the
  Cytoscape network views; `figure5_GO_labels.csv`)
- Supplementary Table 18 (assembled in `10_figure_and_table_generation.Rmd`)
- Methods, "Gene Ontology enrichment of isoform-specific interactors"

## Inputs

- `OUT_MASTER_NETWORK_ANNOT` — high-confidence AP-MS network (one row per bait
  isoform × prey) with the `specificity` label; written by
  `07_apms_scoring_and_network_annotation.Rmd`.
- Gene Ontology annotations from the `org.Hs.eg.db` Bioconductor package (the
  installed version is recorded in the session information at the end).

## Outputs

- `D_GO_PAIR_TABLES/<BAIT>_pathway_details.csv` — all cutoff-passing terms per bait
  (read by `10_figure_and_table_generation.Rmd` for Fig. 5f and Supplementary
  Table 18). Bait names follow the network table (e.g. `NHERF2`, `CFDP1`); display
  symbols are applied downstream.
- `OUT_GO_MASTER_SUMMARY` — top-10 terms per bait × category × ontology.
- `OUT_GO_NETWORK_LABELS` — one function term (BP or MF) and one compartment term
  (CC) per bait per isoform for the Fig. 5g/h labels.

## Run order

Requires `07_apms_scoring_and_network_annotation.Rmd`. Feeds
`10_figure_and_table_generation.Rmd`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}
source("config.R")
library(tidyverse)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

filter <- dplyr::filter
select <- dplyr::select

require_files(OUT_MASTER_NETWORK_ANNOT)
ensure_dir(RES_08, D_GO_PAIR_TABLES)
```

# 1. Load the annotated interaction network

The network table carries one row per bait isoform and prey, with the bait gene in
`source_harmonized`, the prey gene symbol in `target_harmonized` and the
`specificity` label (risk-specific, nonrisk-specific, shared). Only these three
columns are needed here, because enrichment is run on gene sets rather than on
spectral counts.

```{r load_network}
network <- read_csv(OUT_MASTER_NETWORK_ANNOT, show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("source_harmonized", "target_harmonized", "specificity") %in% names(network)))
cat(sprintf("%d interactions across %d baits\n",
            nrow(network), n_distinct(network$source_harmonized)))
```

# 2. Interactor sets per bait pair

For each bait gene, the risk-specific, nonrisk-specific and shared interactors are
collected as three separate gene sets. The shared set is tested in its own right,
because interactors recovered with both isoforms describe the functions the splice
event leaves intact, which is different information from the intersection of the
two isoform-specific term lists.

```{r prepare_gene_pairs}
all_baits <- network %>% pull(source_harmonized) %>% unique() %>% sort()

gene_pair_data <- list()
for (gene in all_baits) {
  gene_network <- network %>% filter(source_harmonized == gene)
  risk_interactors    <- gene_network %>% filter(specificity == "risk-specific")    %>%
    pull(target_harmonized) %>% unique()
  nonrisk_interactors <- gene_network %>% filter(specificity == "nonrisk-specific") %>%
    pull(target_harmonized) %>% unique()
  shared_interactors  <- gene_network %>% filter(specificity == "shared")           %>%
    pull(target_harmonized) %>% unique()

  gene_pair_data[[gene]] <- list(
    risk = risk_interactors, nonrisk = nonrisk_interactors, shared = shared_interactors,
    n_risk = length(risk_interactors), n_nonrisk = length(nonrisk_interactors),
    n_shared = length(shared_interactors)
  )
}

# Set sizes per bait; the Jaccard index is the shared fraction of all interactors.
pair_summary <- tibble(
  Gene      = names(gene_pair_data),
  N_Risk    = sapply(gene_pair_data, function(x) x$n_risk),
  N_NonRisk = sapply(gene_pair_data, function(x) x$n_nonrisk),
  N_Shared  = sapply(gene_pair_data, function(x) x$n_shared),
  Total     = N_Risk + N_NonRisk + N_Shared,
  Jaccard   = round(N_Shared / (N_Risk + N_NonRisk + N_Shared), 3)
) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total))

write_csv(pair_summary, file.path(D_GO_PAIR_TABLES, "pair_summary.csv"))
pair_summary
```

# 3. Enrichment test

Gene symbols are converted to Entrez identifiers with `org.Hs.eg.db`, and
over-representation is tested with `enrichGO` against the default genome-wide
background of the ontology. The thresholds (*P* < 0.05, Benjamini–Hochberg
*q* < 0.2) and the minimum of three mappable genes per set are those stated in
Methods; sets below the minimum return `NULL` so that the per-bait tables simply
omit untestable categories rather than reporting spurious terms.

```{r go_enrichment_function}
run_go_enrichment <- function(genes, ont = "BP", pval = 0.05) {
  if (length(genes) < 3) return(NULL)

  gene_entrez <- tryCatch(
    bitr(genes, fromType = "SYMBOL", toType = "ENTREZID", OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, drop = TRUE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(gene_entrez) || nrow(gene_entrez) < 3) return(NULL)

  enrich_result <- tryCatch(
    enrichGO(
      gene          = gene_entrez$ENTREZID,
      OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
      ont           = ont,
      pAdjustMethod = "BH",
      pvalueCutoff  = pval,
      qvalueCutoff  = 0.2,
      readable      = TRUE
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(enrich_result) || nrow(enrich_result@result) == 0) return(NULL)
  enrich_result
}
```

```{r perform_enrichment}
enrichment_results <- list()

for (gene in names(gene_pair_data)) {
  risk_genes    <- gene_pair_data[[gene]]$risk
  nonrisk_genes <- gene_pair_data[[gene]]$nonrisk
  shared_genes  <- gene_pair_data[[gene]]$shared

  # A bait is only entered if at least one of its three sets is testable.
  if (length(risk_genes) < 3 && length(nonrisk_genes) < 3 && length(shared_genes) < 3) next

  enrichment_results[[gene]] <- list()
  for (ont in c("BP", "MF", "CC")) {
    enrichment_results[[gene]][[ont]] <- list(
      risk    = run_go_enrichment(risk_genes,    ont = ont),
      nonrisk = run_go_enrichment(nonrisk_genes, ont = ont),
      shared  = run_go_enrichment(shared_genes,  ont = ont)
    )
  }
}

cat(sprintf("Enrichment completed for %d bait pairs\n", length(enrichment_results)))
```

# 4. Per-bait term tables (Supplementary Table 18, Fig. 5f)

Every term passing the cutoffs is written per bait, with its category and
ontology, so that the term counts in Fig. 5f and the rows of Supplementary
Table 18 are derived from the same file and cannot drift apart. Files are named by
the bait symbol used in the network table; the figure script maps these to display
symbols.

```{r detailed_pathway_tables}
for (gene in names(enrichment_results)) {
  gene_pathway_details <- list()

  for (ont in c("BP", "MF", "CC")) {
    shared_result <- enrichment_results[[gene]][[ont]]$shared
    if (!is.null(shared_result)) {
      gene_pathway_details[[paste(ont, "shared", sep = "_")]] <-
        as.data.frame(shared_result) %>%
        select(ID, Description, GeneRatio, pvalue, p.adjust) %>%
        mutate(Specificity = "Shared", Ontology = ont)
    }

    risk_result    <- enrichment_results[[gene]][[ont]]$risk
    nonrisk_result <- enrichment_results[[gene]][[ont]]$nonrisk
    if (is.null(risk_result) && is.null(nonrisk_result)) next

    if (!is.null(risk_result)) {
      gene_pathway_details[[paste(ont, "risk", sep = "_")]] <-
        as.data.frame(risk_result) %>%
        select(ID, Description, GeneRatio, pvalue, p.adjust) %>%
        mutate(Specificity = "Risk", Ontology = ont)
    }
    if (!is.null(nonrisk_result)) {
      gene_pathway_details[[paste(ont, "nonrisk", sep = "_")]] <-
        as.data.frame(nonrisk_result) %>%
        select(ID, Description, GeneRatio, pvalue, p.adjust) %>%
        mutate(Specificity = "NonRisk", Ontology = ont)
    }
  }

  if (length(gene_pathway_details) > 0) {
    gene_pathway_table <- bind_rows(gene_pathway_details) %>% arrange(Ontology, pvalue)
    write_csv(gene_pathway_table,
              file.path(D_GO_PAIR_TABLES, sprintf("%s_pathway_details.csv", gene)))
  }
}

cat(sprintf("%d per-bait term tables written to %s\n",
            length(list.files(D_GO_PAIR_TABLES, pattern = "_pathway_details\\.csv$")),
            D_GO_PAIR_TABLES))
```

# 5. Top-10 master table for network labelling

The ten most significant terms per bait × category × ontology are collected into a
single table with the gene and background ratios, because the label-selection rule
below needs the number of supporting interactors and the size of the GO term, which
the per-bait tables do not carry.

```{r master_pathway_summary}
master_pathway_table <- list()

for (gene in names(enrichment_results)) {
  for (ont in c("BP", "MF", "CC")) {
    for (spec in c("risk", "nonrisk", "shared")) {
      res <- enrichment_results[[gene]][[ont]][[spec]]
      if (is.null(res)) next
      spec_label <- c(risk = "Risk", nonrisk = "NonRisk", shared = "Shared")[[spec]]
      master_pathway_table[[paste(gene, ont, spec, sep = "_")]] <-
        as.data.frame(res) %>%
        select(ID, Description, GeneRatio, BgRatio, pvalue, p.adjust, Count) %>%
        mutate(Gene = gene, Ontology = ont, Specificity = spec_label,
               NegLog10P = -log10(pvalue)) %>%
        arrange(pvalue) %>%
        head(10)
    }
  }
}

master_pathways <- bind_rows(master_pathway_table) %>%
  select(Gene, Ontology, Specificity, Description, pvalue, p.adjust,
         NegLog10P, GeneRatio, BgRatio, Count, ID) %>%
  arrange(Gene, Ontology, Specificity, pvalue)

write_csv(master_pathways, OUT_GO_MASTER_SUMMARY)
cat(sprintf("Master table: %d term entries\n", nrow(master_pathways)))
```

# 6. GO-term labels for the Fig. 5g/h network views

One term per bait per isoform is chosen by a fixed rule so that the network labels
are reproducible. Only isoform-specific categories are labelled (shared terms are
excluded because the networks show isoform-specific interactors); a term must be
supported by at least `MIN_COUNT` interactors and belong to a GO category with at
most `MAX_BG` background genes, which removes very broad terms; nested terms with an
identical supporting set are collapsed (proxied by identical bait × category ×
ontology × Count × background size, keeping the most significant); and the top
`TOP_N` function term (BP or MF) and the top `TOP_N` compartment term (CC) are
retained per bait per isoform, ranked by adjusted *P*. Fold enrichment is computed
for inspection only and is not used for ranking, because at Count = 2 it is unstable.

```{r go_label_selection}
MIN_COUNT <- 2      # minimum interactors supporting the term
MAX_BG    <- 450    # maximum background genes in the GO term
TOP_N     <- 1      # labels per ontology group per bait per isoform

stopifnot(all(c("Gene", "Ontology", "Specificity", "Description",
                "p.adjust", "GeneRatio", "BgRatio", "Count") %in% names(master_pathways)))

# Parse "k/n" gene ratios and "K/N" background ratios into integers.
gr <- str_split_fixed(master_pathways$GeneRatio, "/", 2)
bg <- str_split_fixed(master_pathways$BgRatio,   "/", 2)

master <- master_pathways %>%
  mutate(k = as.integer(gr[, 1]), n_set = as.integer(gr[, 2]),
         K = as.integer(bg[, 1]), N_bg  = as.integer(bg[, 2]),
         fold = (k / n_set) / (K / N_bg),
         onto_group = ifelse(Ontology == "CC", "compartment", "function"))

# Steps 1-3: isoform-specific, supported by >= MIN_COUNT interactors, term size <= MAX_BG.
kept <- master %>%
  filter(Specificity != "Shared", Count >= MIN_COUNT, K <= MAX_BG)

# Step 4: collapse nested terms with identical supporting sets, keeping the most significant.
collapsed <- kept %>%
  arrange(p.adjust) %>%
  group_by(Gene, Specificity, Ontology, Count, K) %>%
  filter(row_number() == 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 5: top function term and top compartment term per bait per isoform.
go_labels <- collapsed %>%
  arrange(p.adjust) %>%
  group_by(Gene, Specificity, onto_group) %>%
  filter(row_number() <= TOP_N) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Gene, Specificity, onto_group, p.adjust) %>%
  select(Gene, Specificity, Ontology, onto_group, Description, p.adjust, Count, K, fold)

write_excel_csv(go_labels, OUT_GO_NETWORK_LABELS)

cat(sprintf("%d labels across %d baits\n", nrow(go_labels), n_distinct(go_labels$Gene)))

# Baits without a label on one or both sides are reported so that the network
# legend can state where no term met the criteria.
coverage <- expand_grid(Gene = sort(unique(master$Gene)), Specificity = c("Risk", "NonRisk")) %>%
  left_join(go_labels %>% count(Gene, Specificity, name = "n_labels"),
            by = c("Gene", "Specificity")) %>%
  mutate(n_labels = replace_na(n_labels, 0L))
coverage %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Specificity, values_from = n_labels)
```
